content.title: About
content.content: Passion fruit nectar is a sweet‑tart beverage made from the pulp and juice of passion fruit, diluted with water and sweetened with sugar. It has a vivid tropical aroma and a bright golden‑orange color.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Passion fruit originates from South America but is now cultivated in tropical regions worldwide.
The juice contains over 30 mg of vitamin C per 100 ml, making it a rich source of antioxidants.
Traditionally, passion fruit nectar has been used in Caribbean cuisine as a refreshing drink and dessert ingredient.
Dietary fiber in the fruit pulp supports digestion and gut health.
The nectar is popular in cocktails, smoothies, and marinades for a fruity twist.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity, aids collagen synthesis, and protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids help neutralize free radicals, supporting heart and vascular health.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber and enzymes in passion fruit aid regular bowel movements and may relieve constipation.

items.title: Mood‑enhancing
items.content: The fragrant aroma of passion fruit has calming effects and can reduce stress levels.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal heart function.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The nectar contains added sugar, so people with diabetes or those limiting calories should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Passion fruit allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fruit components.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity can irritate the stomach lining in persons with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Passion fruit nectar can be enjoyed chilled on its own, added to cocktails, smoothies, yogurts, desserts, and sauces. It is also used to drizzle fruit salads or as a marinade for seafood.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the nectar in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C in a sealed container. Once opened, consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if the taste, smell changes or mold appears.
